intro: To filter a database in Notion on Mac, open the database, click the settings menu at the top, then choose View settings > Filter. Pick a property, set the value you want, and choose Save for everyone if your team should see the same rows.

blocks.text: Filtering is the fastest way to turn a long database into a short list. A filter hides rows that do not match your rule. When a row seems gone, a filter is usually the reason, so check the filter menu before you do anything else.
What you need before you start
You need the Notion desktop app for Mac. Notion's system requirements page says the desktop app requires macOS 13 or above. To check your version, open the Apple menu and choose About This Mac.

Notion's official filter help is written the same way for every platform. It does not list Mac-only filter steps, and it does not describe how the Mac app and the web app differ. If a step looks different on your screen, your version of Notion may have changed.
Where the Filter option lives in the Mac app
Open the database. Find the settings menu at the top of it and open it. Under View settings you will find Filter and Sort. Filter sets the rules, and Sort sets the order of the rows that remain.
Filters and sorts are attached to the view you are looking at. If you switch views, the rules you see change with the view. This is the most common reason a filter seems to vanish.

blocks.text: Some guides describe a Filter button in the toolbar, with And and Or toggles. That layout does not match Notion's official wording. If your screen shows a toolbar button instead, follow what you see, and check Notion's help again after you update.
Worked example: show only your open tasks
Say your database tracks tasks with a Status property and an Assignee property. You want to see only the tasks assigned to you that are still open. Start with a simple filter, then add a second rule.
Open View settings, choose Filter, and pick Assignee. Set the value to your own name. Then add a second filter on Status and set it to the value that means still open.

If you pick Me from the person list instead of your name, the filter means whoever is logged in. A teammate who opens the same view gets a different result. Pick your name when you want the list fixed to you.
Save a filter for everyone, or keep it to yourself
When you add a filter, Notion offers Save for everyone. That option is optional. If you skip it, the filter applies only to you, and your teammates see the view without it.
Filters are saved per view. Changes to one view do not carry over to other views. Set the filter on the view your team actually reads, not on a scratch view you use for testing.
Add advanced filters with AND and OR
A simple filter checks one rule. An advanced filter joins rules with AND and OR. Open View settings, choose Filter, then select Add advanced filter.
Filter groups can nest up to three layers deep, according to Notion's help. Fewer layers are easier to read. When a row goes missing, a shallow structure makes the reason much easier to find.
To turn a simple filter into an advanced one, open the edit menu at the top of the database, select Filter, click the filter, then choose ••• > Add to advanced filter.
Sort the rows you filtered
Sorts live under View settings > Sort. Add a sort, then drag the ⋮⋮ handle to reorder several sorts. Click the X next to a sort to remove it.
Sorting and filtering sit in the same menu but do different jobs. When rows look wrong, check both. A grouping setting can also change how rows appear, so check that as well.
Remove or change a filter safely
To delete a filter, open it and choose ••• > Delete filter. To change one, open it and edit the property or the value. Remove filters one at a time to see which rule hides the rows you need.

A third-party guide suggests duplicating a view before you change its filters. Arclet lists View menu > Duplicate view. Notion's help does not document that step, but a copy gives you a safe place to test rules.
Why your database looks empty after you filter

An active filter can hide every row you expect. Connex Digital names three common causes: person filters like Assignee is Me, a filter set to one teammate, and a filter on a property that has changed.

That article cites no Notion documentation, so treat its checklist as a starting point. Its suggested fix is simple. Open the view's Filter menu and remove filters one at a time until the rows return.

items: Using a person filter like Assignee is Me, then sharing the view. Each person sees their own version of that rule.
Saving a filter only for yourself, then wondering why a teammate sees other rows.
Nesting groups deeper than you need. Notion allows up to three layers, but fewer layers are easier to check.
Editing a view you do not use, then looking for the change in the view you do use.
Leaving an old filter on and assuming the database lost data.

blocks.text: Mac app versions and what changed recently

The Mac app is in the 7.x line. Releasebot lists v7.42.1 and v7.42.3, both dated Nov 4, 2026, with a macOS fix for Command Search and Notion AI shortcuts. Releasebot is a third-party aggregator, so confirm the version on your own Mac.
To update, open the Notion menu in the menu bar and choose Check for Updates. If new features do not appear, press ⌘R to refresh the window.

Notion's recent workspace releases do not mention filters. Notion 3.8, dated Oct 13, 2026, covers column-level permissions and synced databases. That release uses a different number from the desktop 7.x builds, so do not mix them up.
Keyboard shortcuts for databases on Mac
Notion's keyboard shortcuts page lists no filter or sort shortcut. You can still move faster. ⌘P or ⌘K opens workspace search, so you can jump to a database by its name.
⌘F searches inside the page you have open. Notion's page does not say how that search treats filtered rows, so do not rely on it to find rows a filter hides.
What to do after your filter works

Save the view you use most, then check that your teammates see the rows you expect. If the database is new to you, read [how to create a database in Notion on Mac](/how-to/create-a-database-in-notion) first.

If teammates need to open the database, read [how to share a page in Notion on Mac](/how-to/share-a-page-in-notion). Sharing and filtering are separate jobs, so test both before you call the view finished.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to filter a database in Notion on Mac?
faq.answer: Notion's official keyboard shortcuts page lists no filter or sort shortcut. Use ⌘P or ⌘K to find the database by name. Then open the settings menu and choose View settings > Filter.

faq.question: Why did my filter disappear when I switched views?
faq.answer: Filters are saved per view. A filter on one view does not carry over to another view. Set the filter on the view you actually use every day.

faq.question: Can I filter on more than one property?
faq.answer: Yes. Add more rules under View settings > Filter. For mixed AND and OR logic, choose Add advanced filter and build groups.

faq.question: How deep can advanced filter groups go?
faq.answer: Notion's help says filter groups can nest up to three layers deep. Keep the structure as shallow as your rule allows, so you can still check it when a row goes missing.

faq.question: Why does my screen show a Filter button in the toolbar?
faq.answer: Some third-party guides describe a toolbar Filter button. Notion's official help describes the settings menu. Update the app, press ⌘R if new features are missing, and follow what your screen shows.

faq.question: Does my filter change what my teammates see?
faq.answer: Only if you choose Save for everyone. Otherwise the filter applies only to you, and your teammates see the view without it.

faq.question: Which Mac do I need for the Notion desktop app?
faq.answer: Notion's system requirements page says the desktop app requires macOS 13 or above. Check your macOS version before you install or update.

faq.question: How do I remove a filter I no longer need?
faq.answer: Open the filter and choose ••• > Delete filter. Then check the rows again to confirm the list shows what you expect.

steps.name: Open the database in the Notion desktop app
steps.text: Open Notion on your Mac and go to the database you want to filter. If you cannot find it in the sidebar, search for its name. Search opens with ⌘P or ⌘K.

steps.name: Open the settings menu at the top of the database
steps.text: Look at the top of the database and find the settings menu. Click it to open the list of view options. View settings lives in this menu.
menuPath: Settings menu at top of database

steps.name: Choose Filter under View settings
steps.text: In the menu, select View settings, then select Filter. This opens the rules you can add to the view you are in.
steps.tip: Filters are saved per view, so confirm you are in the view you want to filter.

steps.name: Pick the property and the value
steps.text: Choose the property you want to filter on, such as Status or Assignee, if your database has them. Then set the value you want to match. For a person property, you can pick a name or Me.
steps.tip: Me means whoever is logged in. A teammate who opens the view gets a different result.

steps.name: Decide whether to save it for everyone
steps.text: Choose Save for everyone if your team should see the same filtered rows. If you leave it off, the filter applies only to you.
steps.tip: Teammates see the view without your filter when you keep it private.

steps.name: Check the rows and close the menu
steps.text: Close the menu and read the rows that remain. If the list looks too short, open Filter again and remove rules one at a time until the rows return.

steps.name: Add an advanced filter for AND and OR logic
steps.text: If one rule is not enough, go back to View settings, choose Filter, then select Add advanced filter. Build groups to combine AND and OR rules. Groups can nest up to three layers deep.

steps.name: Delete a filter you no longer need
steps.text: Open the filter you want to remove, then choose ••• > Delete filter. Check the rows again to confirm the list shows what you expect.

shortcuts.action: Refresh the window after an update

troubleshooting.problem: The database looks empty after I filter it
troubleshooting.fix: Open the view's Filter menu and remove filters one at a time. Person filters like Assignee is Me and filters on a changed property are common causes.

troubleshooting.problem: Filter does not appear under View settings
troubleshooting.fix: Open the Notion menu, choose Check for Updates, then press ⌘R if new features do not appear.

troubleshooting.problem: A teammate sees different rows than I do
troubleshooting.fix: Your filter applies only to you unless you chose Save for everyone. Open Filter again and save it for everyone if the team should share it.

troubleshooting.problem: My filter stopped working after someone edited a property
troubleshooting.fix: Open the Filter menu and check that the property and value still match what you expect. A changed property can break a rule.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot find a row I know is in the database
troubleshooting.fix: Check grouping and sorting, then search with ⌘P. A third-party guide suggests these checks, and Notion's help does not confirm them.

troubleshooting.problem: My filter is in the wrong view
troubleshooting.fix: Filters belong to one view. Check which view you are in, then set the rule on the view your team reads.
